text.p: Greenwich Air Services Inc. said Friday it agred to acquire UNC Inc., an aviation services company, in a deal worth at least $320 million.
Greenwich, which repairs and overhauls gas turbine engines, said it will offer at least $14 worth of its Class B non-voting common stock for each UNC share.
Annapolis, Md.-based UNC's stock soared $2.50 or almost 23 percent to $13.375 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading. Greenwich rose $1.875 to $23.50 on Nasdaq.
If the price for Greenwich's class B stock rises above $24.86, UNC shareholders will receive additional value above $14 per share, up to $16.10 for each UNC share held.
UNC shareholders also have the option of receiving cash in lieu of Greenwich's class B stock up to a maximum of 50 percent of the value of the deal.
Greenwich said the merger will bring the Miami-based company's revenues from commercial aviation engine services and business aviation services to nearly $1.8 billion a year.

"We believe the new combined company will enjoy significant cost-savings in each of our businesses as well as significant opportunities for revenue growth through new business partnerships," Greenwich said.
"These savings and benefits, we believe, will allow this transaction to be accretive to our shareholders after fiscal 1997."
The deal is expected to close in the spring, Greenwich said.
